fullPassage: In the realm of philosophy, it is widely believed that the identity of opposing ideas is inconsequential, as they are constantly changing; in the grand scheme, when one idea changes, another idea arises in opposition to it, continuing the dialogue that drives philosophical progress. However, when looking at social dynamics, this tenet does not hold true, as opposition becomes a stepping stone to conflict. In a political context, especially in situations that bring about questions of social justice, we often grow to view those who hold values in opposition to our own with antagonism and dismiss them as being irrational or immoral. It is not that their perspectives are entirely without merit or reason. It is that we are so fundamentally opposed to their way of thinking that we believe no rational or moral person could hold such beliefs and thus refuse to interact with them, regardless of the quality of their argument. This breakdown in communication can ultimately lead to polarization, or the splitting of a society, making it more difficult to find solutions to social and political issues.

글쓴이는 반대편의 관점이 전적으로 가치도 이유도 없다고 본다.

questions.passage: In philosophy, opposing ideas ①<u>are</u> often seen as unimportant because they constantly change. In society, however, opposition frequently ②<u>becomes</u> a source of conflict. We tend to view people who hold values different from our own ③<u>with</u> antagonism and reject them. This breakdown in communication can ④<u>leading</u> to the splitting of a society.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 어법상 틀린 것을 고르시오.

det.korean: ④ leading → lead: 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형을 써요.
det.analysis:
① are(이다) — 'opposing ideas are often seen' 복수 주어 + 수동태라 적절해요

② becomes(된다) — 'opposition frequently becomes' 단수 주어라 적절해요

③ with(~으로) — 'view ~ with antagonism(적대감을 가지고 보다)' 전치사라 적절해요

④ leading — 'can __________ to the splitting'에서 조동사 can 뒤에는 동사원형이 와야 하므로 lead가 맞아요. leading(분사)은 틀려요 ←정답(틀린 곳)

questions.passage: In the realm of philosophy, it is widely believed that the identity of opposing ideas is inconsequential, as they are constantly changing; in the grand scheme, when one idea changes, another idea arises in opposition to it, continuing the dialogue that drives philosophical progress. However, when looking at social dynamics, this tenet does not hold true, as opposition becomes a stepping stone to conflict. In a political context, especially in situations that bring about questions of social justice, we often grow to view those who hold values in opposition to our own with antagonism and dismiss them as being irrational or immoral. It is not that their perspectives are entirely without merit or reason. It is that we are so fundamentally opposed to their way of thinking that we believe no rational or moral person could hold such beliefs and thus refuse to interact with them, regardless of the quality of their argument. This breakdown in communication can ultimately lead to polarization, or the splitting of a society, making it more difficult to find solutions to social and political issues.
